title: ReviewItem
description: One entry in the review list: something that needs a human, ranked by risk and whether an agent is blocked.

kind.description: pr (agent pull request), approval (an agent waits for permission), question (an agent asks a person), blocked_action (a rule blocked something), exception (a rule blocked a tool call and approving allows that exact call once), stuck_run, budget, spend_spike, quality, policy_report (what an observed rule would have blocked), or context_promotion (a person proposes one of their own context items to the team; approving adds it to the team layer).

title.description: One line shown in the list.

blocking.description: true when an agent is waiting on this answer.

score.description: 0 is safe to skim, 100 needs a careful human read. Drives the ranking.

reasons.description: Plain-language reasons behind the score, most important first.

url.description: Where to act, for example the PR URL.

owners.description: People who should answer, from [review.owners] or the session owner.

version.description: Agent CLI or app version, for example 2.1.0.

name.description: Agent or subagent name when the vendor reports one, for example a Claude Code subagent type.

requested_by.description: For an exception: the person whose agent was blocked. On a team server they cannot approve it unless [review] self_approve_exceptions is true.

run_url.description: The run this item came from in the console's run view, <SELFHOST_PUBLIC_URL>/runs/<session_id>. Added by the team server when the item names a session.

trace_url.description: The same run in the team's tracer, from [integrations.tracer] run_url, once the run has been sent there.

brief.description: Markdown summary of what the reviewer needs to know to decide quickly.

source_event_ids.description: Ledger events this item was built from.

answer.description: The human answer that closed the item.

verdict.description: allow, block and ask come from a rule. approve, deny, answer and override come from a person.

reason.description: Why. For a question, the answer text.

decision_event_id.description: The decision.recorded ledger event that holds this answer.

why.description: Why the item exists: the rule or signal.

signal.description: The ledger signal behind the item: an event kind such as approval.requested, policy.evaluated or pr.opened, or alert.raised:<alert> for an alert.

rule_id.description: Rule from selfhost.toml, when a rule raised the item.

text.description: Why a person is needed, in plain language.

deadline.description: When the item times out. A blocking approval with no answer by then is denied, and the deny is written to the decision log.

actions.description: What a person can do with this item. open needs url.

delivery.description: instant when an agent is blocked or risk is at or above [review] high_risk_threshold, else digest.

group.description: Items from the same run or session share this value: run:<run_id>, else session:<session_id>.

step.description: route (a [[review.routes]] entry), owner ([review.owners] path globs, else the session's person), team (members of the item's team in [teams]), fallback ([review] fallback), or none when selfhost.toml names nobody.

from.description: Where the owners came from, for example [[review.routes]] "db", [review.owners] "db/**", the session's person, [teams.platform] or [review] fallback.

id.description: The [[review.routes]] id, when a route took the item.

why.description: What the route matched on, such as "kind pr, path db/schema.sql, risk 82 at or above 70".

github.description: GitHub accounts the route names, from @ targets and CODEOWNERS, asked to review a pull request.

escalates_at.description: When the item moves on to the next route that matches it (or [review] fallback), from the route's escalate_after_minutes, if nobody answered.

escalated_from.description: Routes the item waited on before this one, oldest first. Their people stay owners.

snoozed_until.description: Snoozed: ranked after every other item until this time.
